# T1917-029 — The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera (Thompson 1917, Ch. XII)

Slot 223 of the Thompson (1917) claim-validation campaign (`thompson1917-t1917-029`).

**Claim (dated 1917, pp. 587-611, Figs. 308-317):** *Foraminiferal shells are generated by
chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the
genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.*

## What Thompson actually measured (pp. 593-595)

| Source quoted by Thompson | Taxon | Series | Stated ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| von Möller (1878) | *Fusulina cylindrica* whorls I-IV | 0.132, 0.195, 0.300, 0.449 mm | 1.5 / whorl |
| von Möller (1878) | *F. böcki* whorls I-V | 0.079, 0.120, 0.180, 0.264, 0.396 mm | 1.5 / whorl |
| von Möller (1878) | *F. cylindrica* opposite half-whorls | 0.096 … 0.395 mm (8 values) | 1.225 / half-whorl (mean Δlog₁₀ = 0.088) |
| van Iterson (1907) | *Triloculina rotunda* chambers 2-10 | 34 … 319 µm | 1.323 / chamber |
| Rhumbler | *Pulvinulina menardii* chambers | — | ≈1.187 / chamber, "small secondary fluctuation" |

Equations, variables, parameter regimes and the five empirical sub-claims (C1-C5) are in
`t1917_029_the_spiral_shells_of_the_foram_reference.json`.

## Dataset (verified, SHA-256 pinned)

**Shi (2021) Paleobiology 47(1):115-133 — Dryad `doi:10.5061/dryad.sn02v6x26` (CC0).**
1396 axial-thin-section test outlines (40 landmarks each) at successive *half-whorl* growth
stages for 106 fusulinid specimens in five genera (*Triticites*, *Pseudoschwagerina*,
*Sphaeroschwagerina*, *Zellia*, *Robustoschwagerina*).

| File | SHA-256 | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `shi2020_dryad_sn02v6x26_Landmarks.dat` | `f7bb3fe7…55c1023` | matches Dryad digest |
| `shi2020_dryad_sn02v6x26_Table_1.csv` | `b5ddc656…a88d` | specimen key (genus, species, code) |

**Match to the claim:** Thompson's only tabulated whorl data are von Möller's *Fusulina*
(fusulinid foraminifera); the Dryad data are fusulinid foraminifera measured as successive
half-whorl outlines — the same "opposite whorls, 180° apart" series Thompson tabulates on
p. 593. Variables and taxon class match; this is **not** a `DATASET_MISMATCH`. Limitation:
whorl-level, not septal-chamber-level; pixel units (scale-free tests only).

## Verdict (Pass 2, pre-registered tests T1–T4): **MIXED** (3/4)

| Test | Result | Numbers |
|---|---|---|
| T1 geometric (log-spiral) succession | pass | median r(ln D, k) = 0.995; BIC geometric > arithmetic in 100 % of 106 specimens |
| T2 near-constant ratio (CV ≤ 0.15 and ≤ 10 % early/mid/late drift in every genus) | **fail** | *Triticites* drift 4.6 %; all four pseudoschwagerine genera 15 % (ratio 1.25 → 1.45 → 1.1 through ontogeny) |
| T3 Thompson/von Möller *Fusulina* ratio 1.225 | pass | *Triticites* 1.239 (95 % CI 1.232–1.245), whorl ratio 1.53 vs 1.5; thin-section CV W = 1.49 ± 0.10 |
| T4 continuous series of genera | pass | Monte-Carlo gap p = 0.74; adjacent genus ranges overlap |

Reading: the logarithmic-spiral / constant-ratio law holds to ~5 % for Thompson's own exemplar group
(triticitid fusulinids) and his printed numbers are reproduced; it fails as a *universal*
constant-ratio law because the inflated pseudoschwagerines (Shi 2021's heterochronic novelty)
change their ratio systematically through ontogeny. Thompson's Fig. 309 *Nummulina* gives
W ≈ 1.61 ± 0.18 by the same CV method — a different constant angle, as his "genera differ in
numerical coefficients" requires.

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 thompson/claims/t1917-029_the-spiral-shells-of-the-foraminifera.py --self-test
python3 thompson/claims/t1917-029_the-spiral-shells-of-the-foraminifera.py            # ~6 s
python3 thompson/claims/t1917-029_the-spiral-shells-of-the-foraminifera.py --fast --no-gif
```
